title: Simply connected semisimple character lattice is the weight lattice
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $G$ be a semisimple simply connected $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]. Semisimple means smooth, connected, affine and of finite type, with no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup. Simply connected means that every surjective homomorphism from a semisimple group with finite central kernel is an isomorphism; finite means finite-dimensional coordinate algebra, and central means commuting after every scalar extension. Fix a split maximal torus $T$ and a Borel subgroup $B\supseteq T$, with character lattice $X$, roots $\Phi$, positive roots $\Phi^+$, simple roots $\Delta=\{\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r\}$ and coroots as in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Put $V=X\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$. The simple roots are a $\mathbf Q$-basis of $V$, their coroots are a basis of the dual root system, and the pairing identifies the actual character lattice with the full weight lattice: $$X=\{v\in V:\langle v,\alpha^\vee\rangle\in\mathbf Z\text{ for every }\alpha\in\Phi\}=\bigoplus_{i=1}^r\mathbf Z\omega_i,$$ where $\langle\omega_i,\alpha_j^\vee\rangle=\delta_{ij}$. In particular each fundamental weight $\omega_i$ is an actual group-scheme character of $T$, including when $F$ has positive characteristic.

proof.text: The Borel-pair structure gives the actual character and cocharacter lattices and their perfect integer pairing, and semisimple implies reductive. Apply the semisimplicity criterion to $G$: the roots span $V=X\otimes\mathbf Q$ and the coroots span $V^*=X_*\otimes\mathbf Q$. The given simple-root base has independent roots and every root or its negative is a nonnegative integral sum of them. The abstract root-base lemma therefore makes the simple roots a rational basis and their coroots a base of the dual root system, with every coroot an integer combination of the simple coroots.

Let $\omega_i\in V$ be the basis dual to the simple coroots and set $P=\{v\in V:\langle v,\alpha^\vee\rangle\in\mathbf Z\text{ for all }\alpha\in\Phi\}$. In dual coordinates, $v=\sum_i\langle v,\alpha_i^\vee\rangle\omega_i$. Since all coroots are integer combinations of simple coroots, this proves $P=\bigoplus_i\mathbf Z\omega_i$. The integer pairing gives $X\subseteq P$. Also $Q=\sum_i\mathbf Z\alpha_i\subseteq X$. The coordinate matrix of the $\alpha_i$ in the $\omega_i$ basis is integral and invertible over $\mathbf Q$; clearing denominators of its inverse gives $nP\subseteq Q$ for some $n>0$. Thus $P/Q$, and hence $P/X$, is finite (it is a quotient of $(\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z)^r$). For $r=0$ these groups are zero and $X=P=0$.

source.place: 22.8--22.9 and C.26, written in dual coordinates

proof.text: The lattice $L=P$ now meets every hypothesis of the lattice-enlargement theorem: it is free of rank $r$, contains $X$ with finite quotient, and every coroot is integer-valued on it by definition. Obtain a split semisimple group $G_P$ and a surjective homomorphism $f:G_P\to G$ with finite central scheme-theoretic kernel, whose torus-character pullback is $X\hookrightarrow P$. Simple connectedness of $G$, with exactly this scheme-theoretic notion of central kernel, forces $f$ to be an isomorphism. The theorem's isomorphism criterion then gives $X=P$. This is the contradiction argument of Milne 23.59 with the lattice enlargement written explicitly.

Combining $X=P$ with the dual-coordinate computation gives the displayed direct-sum formula and $\langle\omega_i,\alpha_j^\vee\rangle=\delta_{ij}$. By the definition $X=X^*(T)=\operatorname{Hom}(T,\mathbf G_m)$ from the Borel-pair statement, each $\omega_i\in X$ is an actual group-scheme character. The argument used integer lattices and central scheme-theoretic kernels, with no separability or characteristic-zero assumption, so this also proves the positive-characteristic clause.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 23.59, with 22.8--22.11 and Appendix C.26; explicit dual-coordinate lattice calculation
